title: Monetary diversity and energy commons
content:
Introducing Marcus Saul, who works with Chris Cook at Island Power, who came up with the original idea for use-credit obligations, a tool that we’re promoting at Growing the Commons, and part of the toolkit that some GtC founder groups are using.

Marcus gave this speech on Sunday 25 October 2026 at the Monetary Diversity Gathering II, at La Tricoterie in Brussels. The slides used appear through the text, in the order they were shown. Originally published on his blog.

Good morning.

I want you to picture a field. A rectangular field of grass. Two goals, one at either end. Eleven players on each side. A round ball.

Two goalkeepers, who are allowed to handle the ball within their own penalty areas. The game is played predominantly with your feet. And the objective is to put the ball into the back of your opponent’s net, for which you score one goal.

We all recognise this game: Football.

Of course, football did not suddenly appear in 1863. Different versions of ball games have existed for centuries. In ancient China, people played a game called Cuju. In Florence, a form of football called Calcio Storico developed and is still played today.
